decisions.facts_regeneration: audit-config.json (env file paths), scan/scan-result.json (skipped-file paths) and runs/d1/banking77/full-r2/kit/results.jsonl (Python tracebacks with file paths; a counted kit result) are inputs of the fact engines, so cleaning them changes the input hashes that facts/facts.json lists. facts/facts-node.json, facts-py.json and facts.json were regenerated with the toolkit's own `proof facts` (both engines must agree byte for byte, or nothing is written); MANIFEST.sha256 with runner/finish.mjs writeManifest. No check was loosened and verify.sh is unchanged. The `facts` object is identical to the original (audit.facts_check.facts_object_identical: 132 facts); only the listed inputs differ, so facts.json's own hash changed from ff6f99318060 (shown on the posted film's verify screen) to 99dc62442173. The counted recordings (wire.jsonl.gz and decide.jsonl.gz of the four counted stages) are byte-identical, so the fingerprints the film shows for them still hold. Records of the original run that cite an old hash were not edited; they are listed under audit.records_left_as_recorded_that_cite_an_old_sha256.
decisions.media: film/film.mp4 and film/poster.png are not rewritten (the cleaning skips media); audit.media_byte_identical_to_source compares them with the originals by sha256.
decisions.toolkit_scope: Exactly the 220 git-tracked files of tools/decide-proof. Excluded because git-ignored: tests/film/out, tests/film-check/work, *.mp4 build outputs, node_modules, caches and test logs.
decisions.kit_and_rows: decide-proof-vd/rows/*.jsonl byte-identical to ~/.cache/decide-proof/rows on the author's machine (sha256 equal to the pins in audit-config.json). decide-proof-vd/kit is `git archive` of apolinario/decision-index at commit 87d4650b42b377c0291a89c1f1a879f9b31082bf (MIT licence file included, runner.py sha256 equals the pin); verify.sh does not read it.
decisions.git_attributes: .gitattributes sets `* -text` so that git never changes line endings: the manifest lists the sha256 of every byte.

scan.what: the toolkit's own scanner, run from tools/decide-proof as: node bin/proof.mjs scan --audit <audit-config.json> --json <out> <paths>; it reads the env files named in the config inside its own process and looks for 143 secret values (plain, URL-encoded, base64 and JSON-escaped forms, inside .gz too); its planted control must pass first

data_scope.paths: data/, decide-proof-vd/rows, README.md, verify-all.sh, LICENSE, LICENSE-DATA.md, .gitattributes

whole_tree.all_hits_are_in: tools/decide-proof (code, docs, tests) and decide-proof-vd/kit only; none in data/, the rows, README, licences or this file
whole_tree.why_they_are_not_secrets: The scanner treats every env variable whose name contains BASE_URL, AUTH, ... as secret. The hit variables are LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL, LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL, TEST_LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL, LLAMACPP_BASE_URL, TEST_LLAMACPP_BASE_URL and OLLAMA_BASE_URL (values classified in-process by a regular expression, never printed: loopback http URLs of 22 to 24 characters, the default local-model server addresses that recorder-config.mjs, shim.mjs and fake-provider.mjs also list as defaults), GOOGLE_AUTH_UNIVERSE_DOMAIN (a 14-character bare public domain name, found in two kit files), and the scanner's own non-loopback IPv4 rule (IPV4_ADDRESS), which fires on the synthetic addresses in lib/mask.mjs and tests/lib/mask.test.mjs (documentation and test vectors of that rule). The scanner is built for audit folders, not for toolkit source.

grep.what: read-only byte search of every plain file and of the decompressed content of every .gz (media searched as raw bytes for the path and user patterns only), run on a fresh git clone of this repository; counts
grep.patterns: the path prefix of a user's home directory; the author's username (case-insensitive); session scratch and per-user temp directory names; three phrases the write-ups must not use (case-insensitive, with a space, hyphen or underscore between the words); IPv4 addresses other than the 127.x loopback range
notes: ipv4_in_mask_files: synthetic addresses (private-range, documentation and test values, and the unspecified address) in the masking rule's own source and tests (lib/mask.mjs, tests/lib/mask.test.mjs); ipv4_elsewhere is the count outside those two files.
The only e-mail-shaped strings in the repository are two test fixtures of the toolkit (t@example.com and a fake proxy credential on a .invalid host).
